Early Pressure and the Woodwork From the opening whistle, Atletico Madrid sought to impose their will on the game in front of 52,643 spectators. The home side pushed forward early, utilizing the creative sparks of Alejandro Baena and Antoine Griezmann . The first major scare for the visitors came in the 12th minute when Ademola Lookman found space in the area and unleashed a powerful strike that beat the goalkeeper but rattled the post. This early warning shot set the tone for a half where the hosts dominated possession but struggled to find the clinical final touch. Alexander Soerloth was a constant aerial threat, testing Ionut Andrei Radu with a firm header in the 29th minute, but the Celta Vigo goalkeeper was well-positioned to make the save. Despite the waves of pressure and a series of corners delivered by Koke , the Celta defense remained organized. Ilaix Moriba saw yellow for a dangerous challenge as the visitors fought to disrupt the flow of the game, successfully keeping the scoreline level heading into the interval. The Moment of Magic The second half began with even higher intensity as Atletico continued their search for an opener. Alexander Soerloth nearly produced a spectacular goal in the 52nd minute with a bicycle kick, but Ionut Andrei Radu produced a brilliant save to deny him. This resilience from the Celta backline laid the foundation for the game's turning point. In the 62nd minute, against the run of play, Williot Swedberg found Borja Iglesias with a pinpoint pass. Iglesias spotted the goalkeeper off his line and executed an exquisite right-footed lob that sailed into the net to give the visitors the lead. The goal prompted a flurry of tactical changes from both benches. Diego Simeone introduced Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada , while Celta brought on the veteran Iago Aspas and Ferran Jutgla to help manage the lead. Atletico 's frustration began to show as Alejandro Baena received a yellow card, and the home side struggled to find the same fluidity they had displayed earlier in the match. Celta's Defensive Resilience The final ten minutes were a frantic affair as Atletico Madrid threw everything forward. Matteo Ruggeri tried his luck from distance, but his effort missed the target. In the 88th minute, Miguel Llorente met a corner from Koke with a header, but once again, Radu was the hero for the visitors, comfortably catching the ball to preserve the advantage. Celta Vigo managed the closing stages with professional discipline, even as the referee added three minutes of stoppage time. Despite the home side finishing with 56% possession and a high volume of set pieces, they could not break through a stubborn defensive wall. When the final whistle blew, the Celta players celebrated a hard-earned victory built on defensive solidity and clinical finishing. The result leaves Atletico reflecting on missed opportunities and the fine margins of top-flight football.

The atmosphere was electric on May 3, 2026 , as Celta Vigo and Elche faced off in a high-stakes La Liga encounter. With both sides desperate to assert their dominance in the mid-table standings, the stage was set for a match defined by tactical shifts, clinical finishing, and high-octane drama. Celta Take Command in the First Half The home side started with intent, and it didn't take long for the deadlock to be broken. In the 14th minute, a defensive lapse by David Affengruber proved costly for Elche . Javi Rueda capitalized on the error, providing the delivery for Hugo Alvarez to tap the ball home with his right foot. The early goal galvanized the home crowd of 15,401, and Celta Vigo continued to press their advantage. The legendary Iago Aspas doubled the lead in the 30th minute, showcasing his trademark class with a clinical strike from outside the box after being set up by Ferran Jutgla . Despite trailing by two, Elche dominated the ball, controlling 67% of possession throughout the match . They searched for a way back into the game before the break, but Celta 's goalkeeper Ionut Andrei Radu remained alert. Just before the halftime whistle, Andre Silva sent a powerful header toward the target, but Radu was positioned perfectly to make a comfortable save, ensuring the hosts went into the tunnel with a two-goal cushion. Elche Fight Back from the Penalty Spot The second half saw a flurry of tactical changes as both managers looked to influence the outcome. Elche ’s persistence finally paid off in the 81st minute when the pressure told on the Celta Vigo defense. Manu Fernandez conceded a penalty for tripping Andre Silva inside the area, leaving the referee with no choice but to point to the spot. Andre Silva took responsibility himself, firing a right-footed shot into the net. Although Radu guessed correctly and came close to denying the effort, the power was enough to bring the visitors within one goal . With the momentum swinging toward the visitors, Celta Vigo looked vulnerable for the first time in the sports contest. The tension was palpable as Yoel Lago received a yellow card for a rough foul just minutes after the restart, reflecting the growing desperation in the home side's defensive ranks. Iglesias Delivers the Decisive Blow However, the drama was far from over. Just three minutes after conceding, Celta Vigo responded with a counter-attack that restored their breathing room. Substitutes Williot Swedberg and Sergio Carreira combined beautifully to slice through the Elche defense, finding Borja Iglesias in the box. The experienced striker made no mistake, finishing with his left foot to make it 3-1. It was a hammer blow for the visitors, who had worked so hard to find a route back into the game. Elche threw everything forward during the six minutes of added time, creating several half- chances . Hector Fort and Lucas Cepeda both attempted ambitious long-range strikes, but neither could find the target. The defensive resolve of Yoel Lago , who made several key clearances and interceptions in the dying moments, ensured that every player in a sky-blue shirt played their part. When the final whistle blew, Celta Vigo celebrated a hard-fought victory, having weathered a storm to secure a vital result in front of their supporters.

The closest either side came to scoring was in the 42nd minute, when Sevilla's Isaac Romero let fly from distance, only to see his effort fizz narrowly wide of the target. Despite an earlier yellow card for a rough foul, Moriba stood tall as the defining figure of the match. Holding Firm Against Pressure Sevilla responded with a series of tactical substitutions, introducing Neal Maupay , Ruben Vargas , and Akor Adams to find a way back. Vargas saw a direct free kick sail wide, while Maupay struggled to deliver quality from set pieces. As the match entered its final stages, Celta Vigo nearly doubled their lead when Hugo Alvarez attempted an audacious bicycle kick that drifted wide. In the dying moments, the tension boiled over as Neal Maupay received a yellow card for unsportsmanlike conduct, leaving the visitors empty-handed as the final whistle blew in front of 20,901 spectators.

Just four minutes into the game, Ferran Jutgla found the back of the net with a clinical right-footed finish, expertly set up by Hugo Alvarez . The hosts looked comfortable for much of the first half, controlling the tempo and keeping the visitors at bay. However, Levante remained patient, waiting for their moment to strike. Levante ’s resilience shone through as they mounted a fierce comeback. With the momentum firmly in their favor, Levante pressed for a winner. It came in the 63rd minute when Jon Olasagasti delivered a perfect corner from the right, allowing Roger Brugue to rise highest and head the ball home. The turnaround was complete, and Levante suddenly found themselves in the driving seat for the final half-hour of the match. Desperate Pressure and Resilient Defense The closing stages were characterized by Celta Vigo ’s relentless pursuit of an equalizer. Managerial changes saw the introduction of Borja Iglesias , Williot Swedberg , and Oscar Mingueza to bolster the attack. Levante nearly added a fourth in the 83rd minute, but Roger Brugue ’s effort rattled the post. Despite ten minutes of stoppage time and several dangerous corners from Swedberg and Mingueza , the Levante defense held firm. Mathew Ryan ’s yellow card for time-wasting highlighted the tension of the final moments. Ultimately, Levante ’s ability to capitalize on defensive lapses proved decisive, securing a hard-fought three points away from home.
